Pattern: merge with + N; merge + N + and + N
Examples: Two regional carriers merged last year. | They merged the two depots to save rent.

Pattern: acquire + N; danh từ acquisition
Examples: The group acquired its main rival in May. | They acquired the licence rather than the factory.

Pattern: liquidate + N (a company, assets)
Examples: The receiver liquidated the remaining assets. | The firm was liquidated within six weeks.

Pattern: devalue + N; thường bị động
Examples: The currency was devalued twice in a year. | Devaluing helped exporters and nobody else.

Definition: nới lỏng, bãi bỏ quy định
Pattern: deregulate + N; thường bị động
Examples: Coach routes were deregulated in the 1980s. | They deregulated lending and then regretted it.

Pattern: forecast + N; quá khứ forecast hoặc forecasted
Examples: The bank forecast growth of one per cent. | Nobody forecast a fall of that size.

Pattern: haggle over + N; haggle with + sb
Examples: Buyers haggle over every crate at dawn. | She haggled with three wholesalers.

Pattern: squander + N + on + N
Examples: The windfall was squandered on consultants. | They squandered a decade of revenue.

Pattern: hoard + N; danh từ a hoard
Examples: Traders hoarded rice until the price doubled. | Households hoarded fuel before the levy.

Pattern: be/become + insolvent
Examples: The club had been insolvent for months. | Two contractors became insolvent mid-project.

Definition: do nhà nước cấp kinh phí
Pattern: a state-funded + N (scheme, body)
Examples: The scheme is state-funded but locally run. | State-funded research produced the patent.

Pattern: a debt-ridden + N (company, economy)
Examples: A debt-ridden airline cannot refit its fleet. | They inherited a debt-ridden estate.

Pattern: a cash-strapped + N (council, firm)
Examples: Cash-strapped councils sold their buildings. | A cash-strapped hospital delays every repair.

Pattern: a labour-intensive + N (industry, process)
Examples: Tea picking remains labour-intensive. | The process is labour-intensive and hard to automate.

Pattern: a capital-intensive + N (sector, project)
Examples: Steel is a capital-intensive business. | Capital-intensive projects need patient money.

Pattern: a thriving + N (market, trade, sector)
Examples: A thriving repair trade grew up beside the plant. | The market square is thriving again.

Definition: chịu ảnh hưởng của suy thoái
Pattern: a recession-hit + N (town, industry)
Examples: Recession-hit towns lost their last bank branch. | The scheme targets recession-hit regions.

Pattern: cash in on + N; không tách được
Examples: Landlords cashed in on the student boom. | Nobody cashed in on the shortage faster than the agencies.

Pattern: plough back + N hoặc plough + N + back; tách được
Examples: They ploughed back every profit for five years. | Surpluses are ploughed back into the kitchen.

Pattern: pull out of + N; không tách được
Examples: The investor pulled out of the deal in June. | Two banks pulled out of the market entirely.

Pattern: pour money into + N; tách được
Examples: The state poured money into the shipyards. | They poured money into advertising and lost it.

Pattern: sell off + N hoặc sell + N + off; tách được
Examples: The board sold off the overseas division. | They sold two depots off to cover the deficit.

Definition: mở rộng sang lĩnh vực mới
Pattern: branch out into + N
Examples: The bakery branched out into catering. | He branched out after the first good year.

Pattern: tighten + one's belt
Examples: Households tightened their belts before the bills arrived. | The ministry was told to tighten its belt again.

Pattern: affect/improve + the bottom line
Examples: Every delay hits the bottom line. | Training improved the bottom line within a year.

Pattern: be/stay + in the red
Examples: The branch has been in the red since 2019. | They stayed in the red for three winters.

Pattern: be in + the black; move into + the black
Examples: Two routes are comfortably in the black. | The company moved into the black last autumn.

Pattern: be/treat sth as + a cash cow
Examples: The car park became a cash cow for the hospital. | Textbooks are a cash cow for publishers.

Definition: chu kì bùng nổ rồi sụp đổ
Pattern: a cycle of + boom and bust
Examples: Housing here runs on boom and bust. | Thirty years of boom and bust taught nobody anything.

Pattern: money talks (không đổi hình thức)
Examples: Money talks loudest at planning hearings. | In that committee money talks and evidence waits.

Pattern: make a killing + on/out of + N
Examples: Early investors made a killing on the flotation. | Someone made a killing out of the land rezoning.

Term: cost an arm and a leg
Pattern: cost + an arm and a leg
Examples: Spare parts for that model cost an arm and a leg. | The repair cost an arm and a leg and lasted a year.
